problem.title: Badge Board
problem.statement: A board sorts 10 badges by two properties. There are 3 red-only badges, 2 badges that are both red and triangular, 4 triangular-only badges, and 1 badge that is neither red nor triangular. How many badges are red or triangular?
hints: Mathematical or includes badges satisfying both properties.
Add the three non-overlapping regions inside at least one circle.

solutionSteps.title: Identify the union
solutionSteps.body: Red or triangular includes red only, both, and triangular only.

solutionSteps.title: Add the regions
solutionSteps.body: The region counts are disjoint, so 3 + 2 + 4 = 9.

solutionSteps.title: Check the universe
solutionSteps.body: The 9 union badges and 1 neither badge account for all 10 badges.

notes: Both independent counts give a nine-badge inclusive union.

problem.title: Pet Register
problem.statement: A neighborhood register shows 5 households with only a cat, 3 with both a cat and a dog, 4 with only a dog, and 2 with neither. How many households are in the intersection of the cat and dog sets?

solutionSteps.title: Locate the intersection
solutionSteps.body: The intersection contains households with both a cat and a dog.

validationMethods: definition check that intersection selects the both region
independent four-region table lookup locating count 3
notes: The question asks for one explicitly stated region, whose count is 3.

problem.title: Recreation Center
problem.statement: At a recreation center, 6 members take only swimming, 2 take both swimming and tennis, 5 take only tennis, and 3 take neither class. How many members take swimming or tennis?
hints: Or includes members taking both classes.
Add each region inside at least one class circle once.

solutionSteps.title: Choose the union regions
solutionSteps.body: Swimming or tennis includes swimming only, both, and tennis only.

notes: The two methods confirm the inclusive union count 13.

problem.title: Marker Sets
problem.statement: A Venn diagram has 7 markers in A only, 4 in both A and B, 6 in B only, and 1 in neither set. How many markers are in set A?
hints: Set A includes its exclusive region and the intersection.
Do not include B only or neither.

solutionSteps.title: Trace circle A
solutionSteps.body: Circle A contains the 7 A-only markers and the 4 shared markers.

notes: Both direct inclusion and outside-A exclusion give 11.

problem.title: Integer Property Board
problem.statement: The integers from 1 through 12 are sorted into set A, the even integers, and set B, the multiples of 3. How many integers are in neither A nor B?
hints: Test each number for both properties.
Neither means odd and not divisible by 3.

solutionSteps.title: Find the outside values
solutionSteps.body: The integers 1, 5, 7, and 11 are odd and not multiples of 3.

solutionSteps.title: Count and check
solutionSteps.body: There are 4 such integers. The other eight appear in at least one set.

validationMethods: exhaustive property testing of all integers 1 through 12
notes: Both enumeration and the complete partition give four outside values.

problem.title: Library Activity Survey
problem.statement: A survey of 28 students places 9 in reading club only, 5 in both reading club and puzzle club, and 8 in puzzle club only. The remaining students are in neither club. How many students are in neither club?
hints: First count the three disjoint regions inside the union.
Subtract that union from the full survey universe.

solutionSteps.title: Count the union
solutionSteps.body: The three inside regions contain 9 + 5 + 8 = 22 students.

solutionSteps.title: Find neither
solutionSteps.body: The remaining 28 − 22 = 6 students are outside both clubs.

validationMethods: independent whole-board equation 9+5+8+n=28 solved as n=6
notes: Both methods account for all 28 students and give 6 in neither.

problem.title: Divisible by Four or Six
problem.statement: How many integers from 1 through 20 are divisible by 4 or divisible by 6?
hints: List the multiples of each divisor through 20.
The shared multiple 12 belongs in the union only once.

solutionSteps.title: List both sets
solutionSteps.body: Multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. Multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18.

solutionSteps.title: Merge the lists
solutionSteps.body: The union is 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 18, 20, with 12 written once.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of the seven-element merged union
independent region count: four multiples of 4 only, one shared multiple, and two multiples of 6 only
notes: Enumeration and the 4+1+2 region count independently give 7.
